parent: Index Medical Ltd (online doctor, Bristol); pharmacy: The Park Road Pharmacy Ltd t/a Dr Fox Pharmacy, Glasgow
model: Low-cost UK online doctor and pharmacy: a one-page yes/no medical form, the patient picks the product, pay per order with no subscription, a doctor approves before despatch.

access.accountWall: After the medical form, the 'Choose treatment' page and the 'Confirm order' basket page: pressing 'Confirm order' ('Next: Register/login and pay') opens https://www.doctorfox.co.uk/order/login ('Please login to continue. Create account or login'). The patient sees the full product list and the total price (for example £14.90 for 28 finasteride tablets) before the wall.
access.coverageNote: The whole medical form (17 questions, one page) is plain HTML on the public hair-loss page and was saved and parsed (quiz-definition.html). Two live walks covered both product routes (Q745 Yes and No) up to the choose page, and one went on to the login page. The registration form was read but not filled. Not tested yet: whether answers that only show a message (Q742, Q743, Q746, Q747) really remove products on the choose page, and anything after sign-in (doctor review, identity checks). There is no women's flow: Dr Fox treats men only.

products.name: Finasteride 1mg tablets (generic)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed for male pattern hair loss (any UK generic: Accord, Amarox, Bristol, Mylan, Milpharm/Aurobindo or Relonchem)
products.priceDetail: 56 tablets £18.80; 84 tablets £26.50; 168 tablets £43.50. Pay per order, no subscription. Plus a prescription fee per order (site code bands on prescription items: £0.01-£9.99 = £1, £10-£19.99 = £2, £20-£39.99 = £3, £40 or more = £4; the public table says 'up to £10 = £1' but a 28-pack at £10.00 was charged £2.00 in the live walk) and £2.90 Royal Mail Tracked 24 delivery. Live walk total for 28 tablets: £14.90.
products.recommendedWhen: Offered on the 'Choose treatment' page when the patient answers No to 'Do you wish to order Dr Fox Dual Action Hair Growth Spray?' and passes every stop question (observed). The form's own messages say it is not supplied if the patient takes dutasteride or finasteride 5 mg, is allergic to finasteride, or has had sexual side effects on a 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor, depression, prostate cancer, gynaecomastia or liver disease (docs; not yet tested live).

products.name: Propecia 1mg tablets (branded finasteride)
products.legalStatus: POM, licensed (brand Propecia; the price table names Merck)
products.priceDetail: 56 tablets £81.70; 84 tablets £108.40; 168 tablets £214.00. Plus prescription fee (£4 for any order of £40 or more) and £2.90 delivery. No subscription.
products.recommendedWhen: Same as generic finasteride: listed beside it on the choose page when the spray is declined (observed). Dr Fox says the generic and the brand are medically the same.

products.name: Dr Fox Dual Action Hair Growth Spray
products.form: scalp spray, 60 ml bottle with atomiser; 6 pumps (1 ml) once a day, so one bottle lasts two months
products.legalStatus: Unlicensed 'special' supplied on prescription, made for Dr Fox by Xeal Pharma (MS 46688), a licensed UK specials manufacturer; patient must agree to off-label/unlicensed supply in the form (Q748). In the choose-page code it is flagged as a non-prescription item for the prescription-fee calculation.
products.price: £26.00 for 60 ml (two months), about £13 a month
products.priceDetail: 2 x 60 ml (four months) £48.00 on the product and price pages but £48.50 on the live choose page; 3 x 60 ml (six months) £72.00. No subscription; 12-month expiry from manufacture. Mainland UK only (flammable, sent by APC courier per the product page; the delivery panel says Royal Mail Tracked 24, £2.90). No prescription fee is added on the choose page because the item is flagged non-prescription in code (final checkout not seen).
products.recommendedWhen: Only when the patient answers Yes to 'Do you wish to order Dr Fox Dual Action Hair Growth Spray?' (Q745); it is then the only product on the choose page (observed). Never sold with finasteride tablets or minoxidil products. The form says it is not supplied after Yes to Q742, Q743 or Q746 (docs, not yet tested live).

products.name: Regaine for Men Extra Strength Scalp Solution 5%
products.form: scalp solution, 1 ml twice a day; 60 ml = one month
products.legalStatus: GSL licensed medicine (emc SmPC 5765), licensed for men aged 18-65; Dr Fox still supplies it only through the doctor-reviewed form, and off-label over 65 (Q748)
products.priceDetail: 3 x 60 ml £64.00; 6 x 60 ml £118.00. Mainland UK only (flammable). No prescription fee in the choose-page code (flagged non-prescription); £2.90 delivery.
products.recommendedWhen: Offered on the choose page when the spray is declined (Q745 = No) (observed). The form says minoxidil products are not prescribed after Yes to Q746 (low blood pressure symptoms) (docs, not yet tested live).

products.name: Regaine for Men Extra Strength Scalp Foam 5%
products.form: scalp foam, twice a day; 73 ml = one month
products.legalStatus: GSL licensed medicine (emc SmPC 5781), licensed for men aged 18-49; Dr Fox supplies it off-label to men aged 50 and over (Q748)
products.priceDetail: 3 x 73 ml £66.00; 6 x 73 ml £122.00. Mainland UK only. No prescription fee in choose-page code; £2.90 delivery.
products.recommendedWhen: Offered on the choose page when the spray is declined (Q745 = No) (observed); same minoxidil exclusions as p4 (docs).

products.name: Sons Minoxidil 5% solution
products.form: scalp spray solution, 1 ml (10 sprays) twice a day; 60 ml = one month
products.legalStatus: GSL licensed medicine (emc SmPC 100306, minoxidil 5% w/v cutaneous spray), licensed for men aged 18-65; supplied through the doctor-reviewed form; off-label over 65 (Q748)
products.priceDetail: 3 x 60 ml £48.75; 6 x 60 ml £89.90. Mainland UK only. No prescription fee in choose-page code; £2.90 delivery.
products.recommendedWhen: Offered on the choose page when the spray is declined (Q745 = No) (observed); same minoxidil exclusions as p4 (docs). Can be ordered with finasteride tablets (up to 4 items per consultation).

flows.name: Male pattern hair loss consultation (consultation id 65)
flows.stagesSummary: 17 yes/no questions on one page (no account, no photos, no age question) → 'Next: choose treatment' → choose page (spray only, or finasteride + minoxidil products, depending on Q745) → 'Confirm items' → confirm order page with total → account wall (login/register: birth gender, date of birth, contact, address, GP) → payment → doctor review → pharmacy despatch (not tested after the wall). Every product page's 'Start order' button leads to this same form.

rules.then: No hair-loss treatment is supplied at all (including topical minoxidil). Women are pointed to their GP and to Regaine for Women from high-street pharmacies (not sold by Dr Fox).
rules.proof: https://www.doctorfox.co.uk/hair-loss-treatments/faqs.html (Can women take...? Can a transgender man take finasteride? What is female pattern hair loss?)

rules.then: Not supplied: the Q754 declaration says 'over 18' and the spray leaflet lists under 18 as a contraindication. The form itself never asks age; date of birth is taken at registration, and no client-side age check was found.

rules.when: Patient is aged 50 or over (Regaine foam) or 66 or over (Regaine or Sons solution)
rules.then: Supplied off-label rather than refused; covered by the blanket consent in Q748 that every patient must give, because the form does not ask age.

rules.when: Patient has difficulty passing urine (slow flow or trouble starting)
rules.then: The hair-loss page says Dr Fox is unable to supply Propecia/finasteride (the spray page only says 'consult your GP'). The form never asks about this, so the rule can only be applied by the doctor or not at all.
rules.proof: https://www.doctorfox.co.uk/hair-loss-treatments/ (medical information: 'Dr Fox is unable to supply Propecia/finasteride if you have ... Difficulty passing urine'); no matching question in quiz-definition.html

rules.when: Hair loss has been rapid and recent (within 12 months)
rules.then: The medical information says such men should not use these treatments (not likely pattern loss). The form's Q741 only asks about rapid loss 'over days or weeks', total alopecia or illness/medicine-caused loss, so a man with 6 months of fast loss is not stopped by the form.
rules.proof: https://www.doctorfox.co.uk/hair-loss-treatments/ ('Who should NOT use male hair growth treatments? Rapid hair loss (within 12 months)') vs question 741 in quiz-definition.html

engineSummary: Dr Fox has no recommendation engine. All 17 questions sit on one page. Eleven of them are hard stops: a wrong answer shows a warning and the form will not submit, but most messages tell the patient they can change the answer. Four answers (Q742, Q743, Q746, Q747) let the patient continue with a message saying certain products will not be supplied; removal from the choose page is applied server-side and still needs testing. One question (Q745) is the product fork: spray only, or tablets plus minoxidil. The patient then picks the product and pack. Age and sex at birth are only checked by declaration in the form and at registration; a doctor approves each order before despatch.
strengths: Lowest prices found in the UK market: finasteride £10 for 28, a triple-active compounded spray at £26 for two months, no subscription.
Total price, including fees and delivery, is shown before any sign-in.
Very open about unlicensed and off-label supply, with explicit consent and clear cautions (PSA, mood, sexual effects, pregnancy handling).
Every exclusion is written in plain words on the form and the product pages.
weaknesses: The form tells patients that a 'wrong' answer can simply be changed to continue, which invites gaming.
No age question and no photos: the norwood stage, pattern and duration are never asked, so diagnosis rests on self-declaration.
Men only: no treatment for women at all, not even topical minoxidil.

Small inconsistencies: spray 2 x 60 ml is £48.00 on the product page but £48.50 at checkout; the prescription fee table says 'up to £10 = £1' but £10 is charged £2; one message reads 'You should can not take'.
No oral minoxidil, dutasteride or combination tablet options, so no step-up for non-responders.

Some published exclusions have no question in the form: difficulty passing urine (finasteride) and hair loss within the last 12 months are listed as reasons not to supply, but the form never asks them.
opportunities: Women's hair loss is left entirely to GPs and high-street Regaine for Women: a gap for a low-cost women's service.
A step-up path (oral minoxidil, stronger topical finasteride) for men who do not respond at 12 months, which Dr Fox tells to stop treatment.
Photo-based progress checks, which Dr Fox does not offer.
